suggested_requirements.text: The system shall track the movement of lapsed quantities in an area including the permit and well that obtained the quantities.
The system shall track the relocation of active water use within the Southern Water Use Caution Area (SWUCA).
The system shall report on the history of irrigation water conserving credits including balance, earned, and used amounts.
The system shall track and report on the history of permitted data such as use type, irrigated acres, and pumpage.
The system shall track and measure alternative source projects including reclaimed water, augmented surface water, and desalination.
The system shall display the spatial impact of a person's application alongside other active applications on-line.
The system shall create a heat map indicating permittees who are over-pumping.
The system shall create a heat map for water quality including District WUPnet sentinel wells.
The system shall report on permits that have been relocated by a permit holder.
The system shall track the impact of water use on established Minimum Flows and Levels (MFL).
The system shall track net benefit changes including relocated permits and change of use type.
The system shall report the net benefit amount in MGD for land use changes and use of lapsed quantities.
The system shall mark permits that have a land use change for potential relocation to public supply utilities.
The system shall create a GIS layer including cones of depression for MFL information.
The system shall report on water use amounts sold or given from one permit to another.
The system shall report on the improvement percentage and cost for mitigation of MFL impacts.
The system shall report on water made available through District water resource development projects.
The system shall report on permit duration and expiration dates.
The system shall allow comparison to adjacent districts' GIS layers.
The system shall report compliance and crop reports on a permit basis.
The system shall report on competing applications including those in modification or expiring.
The system shall provide water levels in relationship to MFL to identify mitigation requirements.
The system shall determine the availability of alternative use supplies such as reclaimed water.
The system shall report the reservation from use amounts allocated to specific participants.
The system shall track ownership of wells or permits over the life of the withdrawal point.
The system shall identify when a standby permit is reactivated due to the loss of alternative quantities.
The system shall provide a heat map showing permit information for specific time periods.
The system shall automate requests for permitted and pumpage quantities at the permit and well level.
The system shall allow users to find existing permits in or near their service area spatially.
The system shall analyze permits using a soils type GIS layer.
The system shall provide printable and customizable maps.
The system shall identify permits on land purchased by governmental agencies for retirement.
The system shall allow querying of data by issue date, expiration date, use type, and permit status.
The system shall generate a well package file for import into groundwater models.
The system shall associate permitted quantities, pumpage quantities, and use code data at the well level.
The system shall track trends in land use and water use changes.
The system shall track water use over time to negotiate new water use based on pumpage trends.
The system shall track withdrawal sources by aquifer or USGS water body.
The system shall display the quantity of pumpage on a map.
The system shall compare the percentage a permit is over-pumping against the regional average for the same use type.
